Name: Pelican Palette
Author: blinxxy
Description:
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54599/54599-1793998496-3067626.png[/img]
[center]
[size=4][i]"Fireflies are pure light on dark. You can't paint them. I keep trying." - Sable[/i][/size]

Pick up a brush. [b]Pelican Palette[/b] adds painting to Stardew Valley: a minigame as hands-on as fishing, a Painting skill, an art supply shop in Cindersap Forest, and Sable, the restorer who runs it.

Set an easel down anywhere (in your farmhouse, by the river, on the summit) and paint what's in front of you: a parsnip, a basket of fruit, a friend who'll sit for you, your horse, the view. Mix your colours against the fading light, copy the picture cell by cell, then sell, gift, frame or varnish what you make.

And from [b]1.3[/b], the valley turns out to have paintings of its own: twenty-one of them, damaged and lost, in the ground, the sea, the mines, the desert and the volcano. The museum sends for a conservator.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54599/54599-1793998504-822404611.png[/img]


[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54599/54599-1793998515-193661369.png[/img]

[quote][b]Margot Pell[/b], the conservator from the Zuzu City Museum of Art: a second romance, with six heart events, a cottage of her own by the river and her own wedding
[b]Twenty-one old paintings[/b] to find, in five sets, and two ways to restore them: Margot for a fee, or yourself at the easel
[b]Painting Mastery[/b] past level 10: Margot's study board fills on your wall as you paint, and her test makes you a conservator
[b]The Master's Easel[/b]: gold paintings made at it come alive when you hang them
[b]The museum's collection[/b]: donate restored paintings to Gunther, earn rewards for every set, and walk through the new Painting Wing
[b]Sixteen frames that do something[/b]: each one hung helps the easels in its room, and the Framer's Bench swaps them
Paint your [b]pet, horse and farm animals[/b]
Easels at [b]Spirit's Eve[/b] and the [b]Moonlight Jellies[/b], and Sable's Winter Star gift
[b]Five painting special orders[/b], one of them Qi's
The [b]portfolio finished[/b], with a gold-leaf frame and a scene on the Summit
[b]Julian buys a painting[/b] once a season
[b]Modes reworked[/b]: Relaxed is Normal with no clock, the new Simplified is the easiest, Hard pays three times, and the mode is a button right on the easel
[b]Zoom[/b] in on big canvases with the mouse wheel[/quote]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54599/54599-1793999227-1551614880.png[/img]

[quote]Mix colours on a fishing-style bar, then copy the reference cell by cell
Paint before the light runs out; every painting gets the light its detail needs
Catch inspiration sparks for more light and a better score
Still lifes of anything in your bag, portraits of friends, the view outdoors, monsters you've slain, your animals, or your own original
Small, medium and large canvases; glazes on medium ones, highlights on large ones
Quality from normal to iridium, set by your accuracy and your skill, and [b]Masterpieces[/b] on linen
Learn colours like recipes; paint from your Palette; grind your own in a Pigment Mill
Five brushes, from hog bristle to iridium, that wear like fishing tackle
Four modes, changed with a click on the easel: Simplified (no clock, free paint), Relaxed (no clock), Normal, and Hard (the light never waits, and paintings are worth three times as much)[/quote]

[quote]A new skill from level 1 to 10, with its own skills-page bar (via SpaceCore)
New tools as you level: broad brush, ruler, mirror, dropper
Bigger canvases, rarer pigments, higher quality
Six professions: Plein Air, Steady Hand, Visionary, Gallerist, Patron's Favorite, Prolific[/quote]

[quote]Past level 10, your painting keeps counting towards Painting Mastery
The morning after you reach 10 (once you've met her), Margot writes with her old [b]study board[/b]: hang it up, and it fills with pinned studies as you improve
She notices each step, and when the board is full she sets you a test at the museum: [i]Zuzu at Dusk[/i], lent by the city.
Pass at gold and you're a conservator: restore the old paintings yourself, at your own easel
The [b]Master's Easel[/b]: more light, and a gold painting made at it is a [b]living masterwork[/b]. Hang it and its water glints, its firelight flickers and its leaves stir; a still life or a portrait catches drifting window light[/quote]

Dug from artifact spots, fished up in treasure chests, found in mine crates, the Skull Cavern and the Volcano, and now and then on the Travelling Cart

Margot restores them for a fee and posts them back; as a conservator you restore them yourself, painting the missing pieces back in from the whole picture

Six paintings bring a living painting, twelve bring Margot's loupe, and all twenty-one bring a paint-tube Junimo

[b]Do I need to start a new save?[/b]
No. Pelican Palette is safe to add to an existing save. The art shop's letter arrives the next morning.

[b]I played 1.2 on Relaxed. What's changed?[/b]
Relaxed is now Normal with no clock: no light meter and sparks that wait for you, but you paint from your Palette, mixed colours dry, and the picture has its glazes and highlights. If you'd rather keep free paint and plain pictures, switch to [i]Simplified[/i] with the mode button beside Begin on the easel.

[b]The minigame is too hard (or too easy)![/b]
Change the mode right on the easel: click the mode button ("Normal") beside Begin on the setup screen, or use Generic Mod Config Menu. [i]Simplified[/i] is the easiest: no clock, free paint that never dries, and plain-paint pictures. [i]Relaxed[/i] is Normal with no clock. [i]Hard[/i] runs the paint out and never pauses the light, and its paintings are worth three times as much; Simplified's are worth half, and Relaxed's 85%. You can also give yourself more light in the config.

[b]How do I meet Margot?[/b]
Find a damaged old painting (your first is guaranteed from Painting level 3: the next artifact spot or fishing treasure chest) and take it to Gunther at the museum. His letter comes the next morning, and she arrives a week after it.

[b]How do I restore old paintings myself?[/b]
Reach Painting level 10 and keep painting: Margot's study board fills as your mastery grows. When it's full, talk to her at the museum and pass her test at gold. Until then, she restores them for a fee.

[b]Where do I get more colours?[/b]
Buy pigments from Sable, or pick up a tube of a colour you don't know: you learn it on the spot. A Pigment Mill grinds tubes from clay, coal, stone, flowers, berries, minerals and gems.

[b]Is it multiplayer compatible?[/b]
Yes. Each player has their own skill, record, mastery, commissions and consignments. Paintings don't move the clock in multiplayer, where time is shared.

[b]Are Sable and Margot romanceable?[/b]
Yes, both, by anyone. Sable uses they/them pronouns, and Margot she/her.

[b]How do I make a Masterpiece?[/b]
From Painting level 8, paint on a linen canvas: iridium quality, five stars, Inspired, and nearly every glaze and highlight in place.

[b]How do I remove it?[/b]
Sell or trash your paintings, easels and art supplies first, then delete the PelicanPalette folder.

[b]Where's the full guide?[/b]
On the [url=https://github.com/blinxxy-0/PelicanPalette/wiki]Pelican Palette wiki[/url]: every item, recipe, pigment, price, frame and heart event.
